title: Projects and workspaces
what: A way to group conversations, files and instructions for one piece of ongoing work, so you do not start from zero each time.
why: Repeated work benefits from stable context: the same instructions, the same reference files, the same tone.
use: Keep a standing brief for a client, course or product.
Store reference documents the assistant should use.
Share a consistent setup with teammates where the plan allows.
test: Create one workspace for a real recurring task.
Add a short instruction and one reference file.
Run the same task twice, with and without the workspace, and compare accuracy and consistency.
risks: Putting confidential material in a shared space
Assuming it has read everything you uploaded
verify: What each product calls this feature and whether your plan includes it

title: File uploads and document analysis
what: Attaching documents, spreadsheets or images so the assistant works from your material instead of general knowledge.
why: Answers grounded in your source are easier to check than answers from memory.
use: Summarise a long report with quotes.
Extract data from a table or PDF.
Ask questions about a contract or policy you have the right to share.
test: Use a document you know well.
Ask for a summary with an exact quote for each point.
Check three quotes against the source and look for what it missed.
risks: Trusting a summary without spot checks
verify: Supported file types and size limits on your plan
How uploaded files are stored and for how long
Whether files are used for training under your settings

title: Memory and personalisation
what: Features that let an assistant remember preferences or facts about you across conversations.
why: Memory can save repeating yourself, but it also changes answers in ways you may not notice.
use: Remember your preferred tone and format.
Keep role context so answers fit your job.
test: Tell it one harmless preference and start a new chat.
See whether and how it applies it.
Find where memories are listed and practise deleting one.
risks: Sensitive details stored longer than you expect
Shared accounts leaking context between people
verify: Whether memory is on by default for your plan
Where to view, edit and delete what is stored
How to switch it off or use temporary chats

title: Agents and automation
what: Assistants that take multi-step actions, use tools, or run tasks for you, rather than only answering questions.
why: Agents can save time on repeatable tasks, and they raise the cost of mistakes because they act.
use: Prepare drafts from a trigger, then wait for approval.
Gather and compare information across sources.
Handle routine steps in a defined process.
test: Start with a task that is reversible and low stakes.
Require approval before anything is sent or changed.
Review every step it took and what it accessed.
risks: Excess access to accounts and data
verify: Which apps and data it can access, and how to revoke access
Logs or history of what it did
